fields.rationale: States cluster around whether they require a mutual/bilateral agreement, accept one-way substantial equivalence, operate via a formal written compact, issue endorsement-style recognition with experience minimums, or only allow reciprocity in emergency/temporary contexts.

assignments.raw_value: Applicant must be licensed as a mechanical administrator or equivalent by another state or territory, meet qualifications established by the department, and have passed an equivalent examination; upon proof, the department shall waive the examination requirement.
Reciprocity agreements may be entered with other states; the certified contractor must have passed the examination, and all certification fees are required to be paid.

Licensure by endorsement or reciprocity available for holders of substantially similar occupational licenses in good standing from other states; entity shall adopt least restrictive rules and may grant temporary/provisional license for 90 days or longer.

Reciprocal state must accept CA licensees; board must determine on a case-by-case basis that the other state's qualifications and good-standing conditions are at least equal to California's. Trade examination may be waived if applicant provides written certification of good standing for the previous five years.

Applicant must present proof of current licensure in good standing in another state, DC, or US territory with substantially similar standards and submit verified evidence per § 1821(a)(3)-(7). If standards are not substantially similar, applicant must have practiced for a minimum of 7 years after licensure.

Applicant must hold a valid license from another state/territory with substantially equivalent criteria, OR have held such license for at least 10 years, OR the other state must have a reciprocal agreement with Florida. Division I contractors and roofing contractors must complete a 2-hour Florida Building Code course.
Reciprocity available by board regulation with states having requirements substantially equal to Georgia's, provided a similar privilege is offered to Georgia residents.

Emergency licensure by endorsement available during declared state of emergency/disaster; requires proof of out-of-state license in good standing for 2 years, liability/property damage insurance, workers' compensation insurance, financial statement, fees, tax clearance, and bond.
Nonresident must be licensed under statutes of another state with similar licensing requirements, and that state must grant the same reciprocal privileges to Iowa residents.

Applicant must hold a comparable classification license in another state; licensing state must certify applicant passed the examination and is in good standing. Trade exam may be waived; business law exam cannot be waived. All other licensing requirements apply unless waived for good cause.

Applicant must pay the application fee, hold an active equivalent license in good standing in the other state, meet MD qualifications including equivalent years of work experience, and the other state must offer reciprocal exam waiver to MD licensees.

Applicant must submit notarized affidavit with education/experience details and notarized statement from governmental official regarding unavailability of foreign records. Military veterans and dependents may obtain licensure without examination if holding equivalent out-of-state license in good standing for at least 1 year with substantially equivalent requirements.
Satisfactory proof that qualifications are substantially equivalent to NC licensees; payment of usual license fee; no written examination required.
Equal reciprocity must be provided to NJ Master HVACR contractors by the applicant's domiciliary state, and the domiciliary state's standards must be equal to or comparable to NJ's standards.
Reciprocal licensing agreement with states having equivalent licensing requirements, entered into by the division with consent of the commission.

License by endorsement available for attainable housing projects in rural areas; applicant must hold valid unrestricted license in another US jurisdiction for at least 4 consecutive years with no disciplinary history. General license by endorsement also available under NRS 622.530 for any applicant with substantially similar qualifications.

Written reciprocity agreement between states must exist; applicant must submit copy of agreement, pay licensure fee, and the specialty section must determine that the other state's requirements are substantially equal to Ohio's and that the other state extends similar reciprocity to Ohio licensees.

Temporary nonresident practice is available only during a declared state of emergency for disaster relief; the out-of-state licensee must apply within 10 days of beginning work, take and pass the examination at the first opportunity, and pay the temporary license fee. This is an emergency exemption, not general reciprocity.

Applicant must hold a license or certificate in good standing in another state with requirements equal to or greater than SC requirements. Board must have authorized an exam waiver agreement. Applicant may be required to pass the SC Commercial Contractors Business, Law and Project Management examination and must comply with all other licensing and certification requirements.
Credit for equivalent experience or equivalent license from another state, as determined by the executive director.

License by endorsement available if the out-of-state license encompasses a similar scope of practice, the applicant has at least one year of experience under that license, and the license is in good standing.

Universal license recognition available if individual holds a current and valid license in another state for at least three years, passed an examination, meets education/training/experience standards, is in good standing, has no disqualifying criminal record, and pays applicable fees.

fields.rationale: States cluster around how broadly or narrowly they define the licensed work: some define HVAC specifically, some fold it into a broader 'mechanical' or multi-trade category, some use a generic specialty-contractor definition, and among HVAC-focused definitions the scope language splits between full-service (design/install/maintain/modify) versus narrower install-and-repair framings.

assignments.raw_value: "mechanical administrator" means a person who is responsible for (A) installing or modifying mechanical piping and systems, devices, fixtures, equipment, or other mechanical materials subject to the Uniform Plumbing Code, Uniform Swimming Pool, Spa, and Hot Tub Code, Uniform Solar Energy Code, and the Uniform Mechanical Code as published by the International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials and the International Conference of Building Officials; or (B) certifying that an installation or modification described in (A) of this paragraph complies with the applicable codes

HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM. A heating or cooling apparatus consisting of an air heating or cooling fixture from pipes, plenums, or blowers, including any accessory and equipment installed in connection within the system. The term does not include window units, automotive, or farm implement type heating or air conditioning equipment.

"Heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration" or "HVACR" means the design, installation, construction, maintenance, service, repair, alteration, or modification of a product or of equipment in heating and air conditioning, refrigeration, ventilation, or process cooling or heating systems

The term 'contractor' includes any person not exempt under Section 7053 who maintains or services air-conditioning, heating, or refrigeration equipment that is a fixed part of the structure to which it is attached.

"Mechanical contractor" means any corporation, association, firm, partnership or other business organization regularly offering to the public the services of its employees licensed to perform plumbing and piping work or heating, piping and cooling work in accordance with the provisions of chapter 393

"HVACR services" means the design, installation, construction, maintenance, service, repair, alteration, or modification of a product or of equipment including gas piping in heating and air conditioning, refrigeration, ventilation, or process cooling or heating systems.

"Class A air-conditioning contractor" means a contractor whose services are unlimited in the execution of contracts requiring the experience, knowledge, and skill to install, maintain, repair, fabricate, alter, extend, or design, if not prohibited by law, central air-conditioning, refrigeration, heating, and ventilating systems, including duct work in connection with a complete system if such duct work is performed by the contractor as necessary to complete an air-distribution system, boiler and unfired pressure vessel systems, and all appurtenances, apparatus, or equipment used in connection

Conditioned air contracting means the installation, repair, or service of conditioned air systems or conditioned air equipment. Service to or installation of the electrical connection between the electrical disconnect and conditioned air equipment is considered to be installation, repair, or service of conditioned air equipment or the conditioned air system. Service to or installation of the electrical circuit from the electrical distribution panel to the conditioned air equipment where the electrical service to the building or site is a single-phase electrical circuit not exceeding 200 ampere

A specialty contractor is a contractor whose operations as such are the performance of construction work requiring special skill such as, but not limited to, electrical, drywall, painting and decorating, landscaping, flooring, carpet laying by any installation method, plumbing, or roofing work, and others whose principal contracting business involves the use of specialized building trades or crafts.

"HVAC" means heating, ventilation, air conditioning, ducted systems, or any type of refrigeration used for food processing or preservation. "HVAC" includes all natural, propane, liquid propane, or other gas lines associated with any component of an HVAC system.

"Heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC)" means and includes the business, trade, practice or work, materials and fixtures used in the design, construction, installation, improvement, extension and alteration of all piping, venting, ductwork, appliances and appurtenances in connection with any heating, ventilation or air conditioning system or subsystems of such.

"Mechanical contractor" means any person who undertakes to, attempts to, or submits a price or bid or offers to construct, supervise, superintend, oversee, direct, perform, or in any manner assume charge of the construction, alteration, repair, improvement, movement, demolition, putting up, tearing down, or furnishing labor, or furnishing labor together with material and equipment, or installing the same for the construction, installation, maintenance, testing, and repair of air conditioning, refrigeration, heating systems, and plumbing for all residential, commercial, and industrial applicati

"Provide heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, or refrigeration services" means to install, maintain, alter, remodel, or repair heating systems, cooling systems, refrigeration systems, ventilation systems, or hydronic systems.

"Heating, ventilating, and air conditioning" or "HVAC" means the application of equipment and systems to provide air conditioning for occupants of buildings and structures. HVAC does not include the installation of portable self-contained refrigeration equipment and window-type air conditioners of not more than 1-1/2 horsepower.
gas, heating, ventilation, cooling, air conditioning, fuel burning, or refrigeration work

The phrase 'heating, group number three' shall be deemed and held to be a direct heating or cooling system of a building that raises or lowers the temperature of the space within the building for the purpose of comfort in which electric heating elements or products of combustion exchange heat either directly with the building supply air or indirectly through a heat exchanger using an air distribution system of ducts and having a mechanical refrigeration capacity of 15 tons or less.

Heating, ventilating, air conditioning and refrigeration contracting means undertaking or advertising to undertake, for a fixed price, fee, commission, or gain of whatever nature, the planning, laying out, installation, construction, maintenance, service, repair, alteration or modification to any portion of any system, product or equipment or appurtenances used for the environmental needs or control of any heating, ventilating, air conditioning and refrigeration system.
Contracting includes constructing, altering, repairing, installing or demolishing any: ... air conditioning, conduit, heating or other similar mechanical works

A specialty contractor is a contractor whose operations as such are the performance of construction work requiring special skill and whose principal contracting business involves the use of specialized building trades or crafts.

"License" means a license the Ohio construction industry licensing board issues to an individual as a heating, ventilating, and air conditioning contractor, refrigeration contractor, electrical contractor, plumbing contractor, or hydronics contractor.

"Mechanical work" means the installation, maintenance, repair, or renovation, in whole or in part, of any heating system, exhaust system, cooling system, mechanical refrigeration system or ventilation system or any equipment or piping carrying chilled water, air for ventilation purposes, or natural gas, or the installation, maintenance, repair, or renovation of process piping used to carry any liquid, substance, or material, including steam and hot water used for space heating purposes not under the jurisdiction of the Department of Labor other than minor repairs to such systems

"Mechanical construction" means the installation, replacement, or repair of plumbing, heating, air conditioning, process piping, refrigeration, lightning protection equipment, or electrical components, fixtures, or devices of any kind, excluding burglar alarm work.

"Air conditioning and refrigeration contracting" means performing or offering to perform the design, installation, construction, repair, maintenance, service, or modification of equipment or a product in an environmental air conditioning system, a commercial refrigeration system, or a process cooling or heating system.

HVAC contractor means a person licensed under this chapter specialized in the installation, maintenance, repair, and servicing of heating, ventilation, air conditioning systems or any other work the division authorizes by rule in accordance with Subsection 58-55-301(4).

"Tradesman" means any individual who engages in, or offers to engage in, work for the general public for compensation in the trades of electrical, plumbing and heating, ventilation and air conditioning.
